title: Mastering Arrays and Array Operations
description: Understanding arrays and common operations on them in JavaScript.

quiz.question: Which of the following is the correct way to declare an array in JavaScript?
quiz.explanation: Arrays in JavaScript are declared using square brackets [].

quiz.question: How do you access the first element of an array named `arr`?
quiz.explanation: Array indexing in JavaScript starts at 0, so `arr[0]` is the first element.

quiz.question: What method removes the last element from an array?
quiz.explanation: `pop()` removes and returns the last element of the array.

quiz.question: Which array method adds one or more elements to the end of an array?
quiz.explanation: `push()` appends elements to the end of the array.

quiz.question: What will be the length of this array: `[1, 2, 3, 4].length`?
quiz.explanation: The `length` property returns the number of elements in the array.

quiz.question: Which method removes the first element from an array?
quiz.explanation: `shift()` removes the first element and shifts the remaining elements.

quiz.question: What does the `slice()` method do in arrays?
options: Returns a shallow copy of a portion of the array
quiz.correctAnswer: Returns a shallow copy of a portion of the array
quiz.explanation: `slice(start, end)` returns a new array from start index to end index (exclusive).

quiz.question: How do you check if a variable is an array in JavaScript?
quiz.explanation: `Array.isArray()` is the recommended way to check for arrays.

quiz.question: Which method combines two or more arrays into one?
quiz.explanation: `concat()` merges arrays without modifying the originals.

quiz.question: What does the `indexOf()` method return if the element is not found?
quiz.explanation: `indexOf()` returns `-1` when the element does not exist in the array.
